# CareSpace architecture

Scope of this build: the agency operator piece. Map what a partner agency can
hold, show the constraint, and hand off to the scan. The network allocator is
the end game and is not built, so the Miramar warehouse is not in the data
either. It is the mother kitchen and belongs to the allocation problem.

## Palette

Sampled from the CareSpace site: brand teal `#377e7f`, white background,
`#1a1a1a` headings, `#555555` body, `#b9d2d2` tint. Defined once as CSS
variables in `globals.css`; nothing uses a Tailwind palette color directly.
The two zones split warm and cool, shelf-stable on an ochre `#b07d3f` and
produce on the brand teal, so the pair reads as two categories rather than two
shades of one.

## Stack

Next.js 16 (App Router), React 19, TypeScript, Tailwind v4. SQLite for data,
generated by a dependency-free Python script.

```
app/
  src/app/                       routes
    page.tsx                     Map Capacity, agency picker (auth out of scope)
    agency/[id]/page.tsx         the reveal, what is on record
    agency/[id]/scan/page.tsx    handoff to the AI piece, stubbed
    agency/[id]/scan/complete/   the after: what it found, inventory check, families
    agency/[id]/scan/fix/        the correction pass, where the rep overrides
  src/components/
    Chrome.tsx                   top bar, badges, section labels
    CapacityChart.tsx            the zone bars with the binding line
  src/lib/
    data.ts                      typed accessors, the only file that touches data
    fixture.json                 generated, do not edit
data/
  schema.sql                     SQLite DDL
  seed.py                        writes carespace.db and fixture.json
  carespace.db                   generated
  README.md                      what is real, what is synthetic, why
```

The UI reads `fixture.json` today rather than the database, so there is no
runtime dependency to wire up mid-hackathon. `src/lib/data.ts` is the seam. To
move onto SQLite, change that one file. The fixture is generated straight out
of the database by the same script, so the shapes already match.

## Flow

```
/  Map Capacity
     └─ pick an agency ──► /agency/[id]/scan          walk the room
                                │                     (camera, not built)
                                ▼
                           .../scan/complete          what the scan found
                                │                     does it square with inventory
                                │                     FAMILIES YOU CAN FEED
                                ├─► .../scan/fix      size, fit, exists or not
                                ▼                     live families recount
                           /agency/[id]               the reveal, why not more
                                                      boxes it holds today
                                                      zone bars, binding zone
                                                      stranded slots
                                                      what one more unit unlocks
```

Phone shaped throughout, because the scan happens standing in a pantry holding
a phone. On desktop it sits in a device frame for demos.

## The model

A Family Box is atomic. It must be assembled at one site from both zones, so a
site's capacity is `min` across zones, not the sum:

```
boxes_today = min over zones of floor(usable_cuft / cuft_per_box)
```

Everything above that minimum in a non-binding zone is stranded: physically
real, permanently unreachable. That number is the product.

Capacity is in cubic feet and inventory is in pounds, bridged by
`item.unit_volume_cuft`. See `data/README.md` for why.

## Where the AI goes

One place, deliberately. The scan is the intake path; nothing else in the
current build uses a model.

The interaction copies Google's document scanner: hold the camera up, the app
hunts for storage in the live frame, and it captures on its own when confident.
The person walks the room instead of filling in a form.

Per detection it produces a form factor, a cubic foot estimate, a zone, and a
confidence score, writing to `scan_detection`. An accepted detection becomes a
`storage_unit` plus a fresh `capacity_snapshot` with `source = 'scan'`.

Three rules for that step:

1. **The human always wins.** A rep correction writes `source = 'override'`
   with a `reason` and supersedes the scan. The scan's number is a default, not
   a verdict.
2. **Disagreement is surfaced, never silent.** If the scan contradicts what is
   on record, ask. Do not overwrite quietly.
3. **Confidence is shown.** Anything under 0.80 is flagged on the complete
   screen so a rep knows where to look.
4. **Two different uncertainties, shown separately.** Detection confidence is
   the model's own, and a rep cannot drag it. Fit factor is a fact about the
   room, and the rep is the only one who knows it. Collapsing them into one
   percentage teaches the wrong thing.
5. **Bias low.** Overestimating capacity ships boxes a site cannot store, and
   that food gets thrown out. Underestimating just moves slightly fewer boxes.
   The costs are asymmetric, so the estimate should be too.

`scan_detection` keeps both the detected value and the corrected value, which
makes override rate per zone the eval metric with no extra instrumentation.

## The correction pass

`/agency/[id]/scan/fix` is where the rep overrides the scan. Three things can
change: how big a unit is, what fraction of it can actually be stacked into,
and whether it is there at all. Plus anything the scan walked past.

A save would write:

| Change | Rows |
|---|---|
| Size or fit edited | `UPDATE storage_unit` |
| Marked not there | `UPDATE storage_unit SET is_active = 0` |
| Added by hand | `INSERT storage_unit` with `source = 'manual'` |
| Any of the above | `INSERT capacity_snapshot` with `source = 'override'`, superseding today's scan, one per zone touched |
| Always | `scan_detection` keeps the model's original guess next to the corrected value |

The families count recomputes on every keystroke, so the rep sees what their
correction costs or buys before committing to it. That is the whole argument
for the fit slider: it makes an invisible assumption visible and arguable.

## Deliberately not built

- Auth. The agency picker stands in.
- The network allocator. It is the end game and needs its own design pass.
- The scan itself. `/scan/complete` assumes it already ran.
- Any write path. `/scan/fix` recomputes live in React state and says exactly
  what it would write, but nothing is persisted.
- Expiration and turnover. Capacity is modeled as static, which is fine for a
  snapshot and wrong for allocation.

## Open risks

- `usable_pct` is a flat per-form-factor assumption. If a scan cannot estimate
  the real fit, every number inherits that error. This dominates the error
  budget.
- One box template. A senior box or an infant kit has a different zone mix and
  would move every binding zone in the table.
- Vida Nueva sits at 40 shelf-stable against 26 produce, only a 1.6x gap. That
  is the one site where a sloppy estimate could flip which zone binds. Every
  other site has a gap wide enough to survive being badly wrong.
- The suggestion engine assumes an added unit is usable at 0.75. It also
  assumes a site has floor space and power for it, which is exactly the kind of
  thing only the rep knows.
